summary: This is South Korean Interim Government Activities No. 25 for October 1947, prepared in Korea by the National Economic Board for USAMGIK. It opens with an editorial on poor integration among SKIG agencies and covers population and repatriation, vested property, food supply, prices, agriculture, mining, industry, trade, labor, public services, finance, government and politics, and social matters. The dominant concerns are the 1947 rice collection and the contested rice price, with a falling rice stock, a 30 October National Economic Board session and legislative wrangling over collection law. Politically it records the appointment of Maj. Gen. William F. Dean as Military Governor, the Russian troop withdrawal proposal, the general election and UN representation debates, leftist and rightist clashes, and the Korean National Youth anniversary. Historians will find dense statistical tables, import and allocation detail from the Civilian Supply Program, financial data, and records of Assembly proceedings and press opinion.
highlights: Hodge announced on 30 October 1947 that Maj. Gen. William F. Dean would become Military Governor of Korea.

Summer grain collection reached 1,237,576 hectoliters, 97.1 percent of quota, though Cheju-do managed only 16.4 percent, while polished rice stocks fell from 1,851,049 hl in June to 434,955 in October.

The rice selling price was raised from 85 to 120 won per small mal against a 640 won per bag purchase price, projecting a 1.06 billion won deficit, as debated at the 30 October National Economic Board session.
The final 1947 rice estimate was 24,930,000 hectoliters of brown rice, about 15 percent above 1946; only 3.2 percent of the 5,156,000 suk quota was collected by 5 November.
Executive Order No. 8 of 20 October restricted rice transportation; the Legislative Assembly voted to rescind it and debated rival rice collection laws, and most papers attacked the ban.
Bank of Chosun note issue rose almost 1.4 billion won in October to 21.8 billion, driven by rice collection and deficit spending, with the 1947/48 budget at 18.79 billion won.
Alien registration in Japan counted 458,359 Koreans by 15 September, and Korean National Youth membership rose from 157,218 to 290,333 between 31 July and 31 October.
A 21-24 October Pyongyang conference fixed payment for North Korean electric power in goods at controlled ceiling prices; use from August 1945 to May 1947 totaled 837,678,737 KWH.

sections.title: Front matter
sections.summary: Cover of South Korean Interim Government Activities No. 25 (October 1947), prepared by the National Economic Board, with blank pages and a contents list of Parts I to VI.

sections.title: Explanations and Implications
sections.summary: Editors call this the second monthly report produced wholly in Korea. They say poor integration among SKIG departments, such as competing claims on electric power and bituminous coal, limits the report.

sections.title: Part I: Basic Aspects
sections.summary: Population movement and repatriation (458,359 Koreans registered in Japan) and vested property, including a 56,730-piece Kangwon-do inventory and six loans guaranteed totaling 361,850,000 won.

sections.title: Section 1: Population
sections.summary: Since 15 October 1945, 885,667 left and 2,342,852 entered; 21,363 Koreans were caught entering Japan illegally. Northern refugees numbered 9,661 in October, and 458,359 Koreans registered in Japan.

sections.title: Section 2: Vested Property
sections.summary: The Office of Property Custody completed a Kangwon-do inventory of 56,730 pieces of former Japanese property, guaranteed six loans totaling 361,850,000 won, and planned a 150 million won rehabilitation of 12 textile units.

sections.title: Part II: Production and Supply
sections.summary: Food supply, prices, agriculture, mining, industry, allocation, trade and labor: summer grain reached 97.1 percent of quota, rice price rose to 120 won per small mal, and 64,588 tons of coal arrived from Japan.

sections.title: Section 1: Food Supply
sections.summary: Summer grain collection reached 1,237,576 hectoliters, 97.1 percent of quota, with Cheju-do at 16.4 percent. Polished rice stocks fell from 1,851,049 hl in June to 434,955 in October; Executive Order No. 8 restricted rice transport.

sections.title: Section 2: Prices
sections.summary: The 30 October National Economic Board minutes defended the 640 won per bag purchase price and 120 won per small mal selling price, projecting a 1.06 billion won deficit. Seoul price indices and coal and tobacco actions are also reported.

sections.title: Section 3: Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries
sections.summary: Final 1947 rice estimate is 24,930,000 hectoliters of brown rice, about 15 percent above 1946. Cotton fell to 42,125,574 kg and cocoon collection reached 45.6 percent of goal; irrigation budget was 967 million won.

sections.title: Section 4: Mining and Minerals
sections.summary: Anthracite output rose to 32,395 tons in September from 21,043 in August. Yong Wol mine could reach 100,000 tons monthly with a 24-mile railroad; bituminous coal from Japan was 64,588 tons in October.

sections.title: Section 5: Industrial Production
sections.summary: September flour output was 430.4 tons, up 83 percent, and machine-made paper reached 375.1 tons, the highest since November 1946. Onada cement fell 44 percent and firebrick 72 percent; Inchon welding plant began making nails.

sections.title: Section 6: Allocation and Distribution
sections.summary: Commerce made 367 civilian supply allocations in September and 837 in October. FFA spent 66,697,000 won in October, FDA sales to provinces reached 269,575,779 won, and the salt kimchi ration was cut to 2.7 kg.

sections.title: Section 7: Import and Export
sections.summary: October private trade nearly balanced on permit estimates: 270 million won imports, 283 million exports. Covers trade with the U.S., Japan, Hong Kong and Egypt, Civilian Supply Program IV, and 64,588 tons of imported coal.

sections.title: Section 8: Labor
sections.summary: National Labor Week opened 20 October; a Seoul employee survey counted 59,009 workers. Rightist and leftist unions contested Pusan seamen, two employers faced court for hours violations, and about 15 plants had health inspections.

sections.title: Part III: Public Services
sections.summary: Transportation, communications, utilities, public works and housing: a 50 percent freight-rate rise lifted revenue, 55 percent of locomotives stayed idle, postal rates doubled on 1 October, and the housing agency finished 11 prefabricated houses.

sections.title: Section 1: Transportation
sections.summary: Department revenue rose 7 percent in September after the 20 August 50 percent freight-rate rise; expenditures rose 18 percent. 55 percent of locomotives stayed inoperative, and a three-day Pusan stevedore strike won a 29 percent increase.

sections.title: Section 2: Communications
sections.summary: Revenue rose from 31.9 to 35.8 million won in September while expenditures rose 72 percent to 74 million won. Staff fell by 4,466 since April, and postal rates doubled on 1 October.

sections.title: Section 3: Public Utilities
sections.summary: Power delivered from North Korea rose 25 percent in October to 55 million kWh of 80 million total. Seoul ran 130 streetcars carrying about 500,000 passengers daily, and 23 trucks were converted to busses in 1947.

sections.title: Section 4: Public Works
sections.summary: October public works reached 150,839 man-days and 26.75 million won in wages, the highest since May. Yong Dong Po to Si Hung highway resurfacing began, and Han River pipeline repairs found 290 leaks.

sections.title: Section 5: Housing
sections.summary: The National Housing Administration finished 11 prefabricated low-cost houses at Yong Dong Po, shifting design from 8 to 7 pyung. A forty-house project with Seoul is planned; Seoul completed its 400-house project.

sections.title: Part IV: Finance
sections.summary: Government and non-government finance: Bank of Chosun note issue reached 21.8 billion won, the 1947/48 budget stood at 18.79 billion, and deposit balances rose to 34.4 billion won.

sections.title: Section 1: Government Finance
sections.summary: Bank of Chosun note issue rose almost 1.4 billion won in October to 21.8 billion, driven by rice collection. The 1947/48 budget was 18.79 billion won with 3.3 billion more requested; excess government withdrawals reached 19,859 million.

sections.title: Section 2: Non-Government Finance
sections.summary: Deposit balances rose 3.6 billion to 34.4 billion won, with the Bank of Chosun holding 53 percent; loans outstanding reached 14.3 billion. Credit lines of 12 billion won were arranged for rice collection.

sections.title: Part V: Government and Politics
sections.summary: Administration, legislature, politics, security, police, interzone and legal affairs: Dean named Military Governor on 30 October, Assembly debated rice collection laws, and the Pyongyang conference set power payment in goods.

sections.title: Section 1: Administration
sections.summary: Hodge announced on 30 October that Maj. Gen. William F. Dean would become Military Governor. Hodge's and Helmick's Korean National Youth speeches are reprinted, with Executive Orders 6 and 7 and the 640-won rice price session.

sections.title: Section 2: Korean Interim Legislative Assembly
sections.summary: In 16 sessions averaging 66 members, the Assembly forwarded Rhee's UN delegate petition 34 to 7, debated rival rice collection laws, voted to rescind Executive Order No. 8, and approved Lee Choon Ho as Seoul National University president.

sections.title: Section 3: Political Developments
sections.summary: Politics centered on Rhee as UN representative, election timing and the Russian withdrawal proposal. Moderates formed the National Independence Federation under Kimm Kiu Sic; release of the 15 August riot plan prompted demands to disband leftist groups.

sections.title: Section 4: Internal Security
sections.summary: The Department of Internal Security comprises the Coast Guard and Constabulary. Pusan harbor block boarded 436 vessels in one week and 672 the next; Constabulary guarded supply areas including the Pusan coal pile.

sections.title: Section 5: Police
sections.summary: Police Director Chough marked the force's second anniversary and warned of a difficult rice collection. Executive Order No. 8 and citizen quota committees aimed to curb abuses; labor party arrests, clashes and three murders were reported.

sections.title: Section 6: Interzone Activities
sections.summary: North Korean power use from 16 August 1945 to 31 May 1947 was 837,678,737 KWH. A 21-24 October Pyongyang conference fixed payment in goods at ceiling prices; mail exchanged 18 October included 6,348 letters from the South.

sections.title: Section 7: Legal Affairs
sections.summary: Covers air mail Order No. 19, Ordinance No. 150 on gold transactions and Executive Order No. 8 on rice transport. Prisoners numbered 20,652, and 54 of 700 applicants passed the bar.

sections.title: Part VI: Social
sections.summary: Health, education, information, press and youth: cholera in Sanchong, 12,452 schools with 3,122,140 pupils, 1,060,000 copies of Hodge's letter dropped by air, and Korean National Youth membership of 290,333.

sections.title: Section 1: Public Health and Welfare
sections.summary: A cholera outbreak in Sanchong had 14 cases and 6 deaths. Other items include six leper clinics, swine plague treated with sulfanilamide, 19,707 refugee dwellings, camp winterization and Women's Bureau committees.

sections.title: Section 2: Education
sections.summary: South Korea had 12,452 schools and 3,122,140 pupils; textbook printing fell to 339,754 for lack of paper. Covers Rockefeller scholarships, the Korea University incident and Cheju-do's severe teacher shortage.

sections.title: Section 3: Public Information
sections.summary: The Department of Public Information released 95 news items and printed one issue of Farmers Weekly. 1,060,000 copies of Hodge's letter on the UN proposal were dropped by air; it also reports 11 radio stations and 65 theaters.

sections.title: Section 4: Press and Public Opinion
sections.summary: The press debated the Russian troop withdrawal proposal, with leftist Dok Lib Sinbo praising the Soviet plan. Rhee's 18 October election call was quoted; most papers attacked the rice transport ban.

sections.title: Section 5: Korean National Youth, Inc.
sections.summary: Helmick's 20 October memorandum called Korean National Youth an official non-political activity for ages 18 to 35, led by Lee Bum Suk. Membership rose from 157,218 on 31 July to 290,333 on 31 October.

sections.title: Back matter
sections.summary: Blank or nearly blank pages 328 to 333, holding only Google digitization notices, a library barcode and a due-date slip stamped June 23 2010.
